title: DBMS Arena Knowledge Content and Challenge Test Accuracy Audit
dataSource: MongoDB Atlas is the running application source; the local SQLite curriculum was reconciled to MongoDB. Verified matching by unit/order/title for all concepts and by unit/concept/type/prompt for questions.

items: Historical lesson and test wording conflated Codd’s 1970 relational model with later SQL development and implied older navigational systems were replaced.
Tier deployment architecture and ANSI-SPARC three-schema abstraction were conflated.
DBMS capabilities were described as unconditional guarantees for consistency, concurrency, access control, and recovery.
DQL/DML taxonomy was presented as universal although sources use different classifications.
EXISTS performance and early-stop behavior were stated too universally.
ANY examples used non-standard list syntax and omitted empty-set/NULL semantics.
ALL examples omitted empty-set/NULL semantics and SQLite syntax limitations.
SQLite database-container descriptions implied server-style permissions and isolation boundaries.
DROP DATABASE wording implied IF EXISTS makes destructive commands safe.
SQLite DROP TABLE question omitted foreign-key action assumptions.
SQLite ALTER TABLE NOT NULL/DEFAULT limitation was described too broadly and incompletely.
Constraint integrity claims omitted engine enforcement/configuration conditions.
UNIQUE NULL behavior was not qualified by engine.
PRIMARY KEY non-NULL behavior omitted SQLite’s documented legacy exception.
Foreign-key enforcement in SQLite was described without noting it is disabled by default per connection.
CHECK wording omitted that UNKNOWN/NULL may pass unless NOT NULL is also enforced.
Index performance gains were stated as guaranteed rather than planner/workload-dependent.
Generated-key language implied gap-free sequences and blurred engine-specific behavior.
Date guidance implied all SQL engines share native date storage; SQLite has no dedicated date/time type.
Relational set compatibility wording suggested column names must match.
Selection-pushdown equivalence was stated without predicate/semantics conditions.
SQL was described as a literal practical superset of relational algebra and calculus.
ACID isolation and durability were overstated as serial execution and crash-proof behavior at all isolation/configuration levels.
1NF definition treated a declared primary key as part of the normal-form rule.
2NF wording focused only on the declared primary key and ignored composite alternate candidate keys.
BCNF example/outcome did not demonstrate a non-superkey determinant violating BCNF.
Concurrency-control definition implied all conflicting writes are prevented from overwriting, independent of the engine’s isolation/locking behavior.
Index introduction used an unconditional large-table performance analogy rather than explaining selectivity and query-planner choice.
UNIQUE introduction implied duplicate values are universally rejected without clarifying engine-specific NULL behavior.

aiGeneratedQuestions.currentControls: AI prompts require an authoritative source title/URL; server normalization requires HTTPS from the trusted-host allowlist and derives correctIndex from the exact correctAnswer option value, rejecting unmatched values. Regression-tested.
aiGeneratedQuestions.limitation: The generator does not fetch and independently verify that the cited page supports the generated claim. Treat AI-generated factual questions as requiring human review before using them as authoritative scored tests.
